content.equation:
Actual Elimination Rate Constant (Ke)
Ke = [ln(Cp ÷ Ctr)] ÷ (Ttr - Tp)
Cp = measured peak level drawn
Tp = hours after dose started to infuse (usually shortly after end of infusion)
Ctr = measured trough level drawn
Ttr = hours after dose started to infuse (usually shortly before next dose)
Half-Life (t)
t = 0.693 ÷ Ke
Ke = elimination rate constant (hour-1)
Volume of Distribution (Vd)
Vd = (MD ÷ 0.5) x [1 - e(-Ke x 0.5)] ÷ (Ke x [Cp ÷ e (-Ke x T1) - Ctr x e(-Ke x T2)])
MD = current maintenance dose
Ke = elimination rate constant
Cp = measured peak level drawn
Ctr = measured trough level drawn
T1 = time between end of infusion and measured peak level (Tp - 0.5)
T2 = time between measured trough level and next dose (tau - Ttr)
Suggested Interval (tau)
tau = [ln(Cdp ÷ Cdtr) ÷ Ke] + 0.5
Cdp = desired peak
Cdp = desired peak
Cdtr = desired trough
Ke = elimination rate constant
Note: Suggested dosing interval rounded to 8, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, 72 hours
Suggested Dose (MD)
MD = 0.5 x Ke x Vd x Cdp x [1 - e(-Ke x tau)] ÷ [1 - e(-Ke x 0.5)]
Ke = elimination rate constant
Vd = volume of distribution in L
Cdp = desired peak in mg/L
tau = suggested interval
Note:Suggested dose rounding:
Amikacin rounded to nearest 25 mg
Gentamicin/tobramycin rounded to nearest 10 mg
Calculated Clcr From Ke
Clcr = (Ke - 0.014) ÷ 0.00293
It has been documented, particularly in a critical care setting, that the calculated Ke can be used to estimate Clcr. This may be used to determine whether
dosage adjustments should be considered for other renally-adjusted medications (Zarowitz, 1992).

content.instructions: To perform a calculation, enter the required variables. Once all the inputs are entered, click the "Calculate" button to perform the calculation. Any time an input variable is adjusted, the "Calculate" button must be clicked to populate the new output. To start over, click the "Reset" button to clear all values and begin the calculation again. Examples for Inputting Patient Information Patient information: Drug: Gentamicin Lab results: Peak: 12 mcg/mL; trough: 3 mcg/mL Dose administered at 0900; peak level drawn at 1100; trough level drawn at 2000 Current dose: 160 mg; current interval: 12 hours Desired peak: 8 mcg/mL; desired trough: 1 mcg/mL How to input into calculator: Drug: Select gentamicin from the drop down list. Measured peak level (Cp): Enter 12 mcg/mL. Hours after dose (Tp): Enter 2 hours (1100 - 0900). Measured trough level (Ctr): Enter 3 mcg/mL. Hours after dose (Ttr): Enter 11 hours (2000 - 0900). Current dosing interval (tau): Enter 12 hours. Current dose (MD): Enter 160 mg. Desired peak (Cdp): Enter 8 mcg/mL. Desired peak (Cdp): Enter 8 mcg/mL. Desired trough (Cdtr): Enter 1 mcg/mL. Detail: Select show if you would like Ke, half-life, Vd, calculated Clcr, calculated dose, and calculated interval to display along with suggested dose and interval. Select hide if you just want suggested dose and interval to display. Click calculate Once a patient is at steady state (usually around the third dose in patients with a stable Scr), levels can be drawn to determine accuracy of empiric dosing. A peak level should be drawn 30 minutes after the end of the 30-minute infusion and a trough level just before the next dose is due. Therapeutic peaks are usually 15-40 mcg/mL for amikacin and 4-10 mcg/mL for gentamicin and tobramycin. Therapeutic troughs are 1-8 mcg/mL for amikacin and 0.5-2 mcg/mL for gentamicin and tobramycin. The toxic effects of aminoglycosides include ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity.
